diagnoses.summary: PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure/PCV signals with high T2 and SPE. The fixed-rule hypotheses point to H2 PCV issues causing elevated reactor pressure. Sensor bias is plausible but secondary.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor pressure behavior, with the strongest contribution from the CSTR pressure measurement and H2 vent activity. This points to an H2 PCV (vent valve) abnormality, most likely stuck closed, causing reactor pressure to rise and drive compensations upstream.
Abnormal PCA with large, coherent upset involving reactor H2 vent and pressure; most likely H2 PCV related fault(s) causing high reactor pressure and compensatory controller actions.

Abnormal PCA with large, coherent movement (high T², high SPE) dominated by reactor pressure signal and PCV-related control actions. Most likely an H2 PCV fault causing a pressure buildup and compensatory control action.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset dominated by the H2 purge/PCV regulation path, with reactor pressure rising and PCV-related signals driving large SPE contributions. The fixed rule suggests a problem with the hydrogen purge (H2 PCV) path, most consistent with the PCV valve fault stuck-closed or degraded capacity, causing reactor pressure buildup and vent/supply deviations.
PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with strong contribution from the H2 PCV loop; high T² and high SPE indicate an actuator issue with the PCV rather than a purely sensor fault.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated, driven largely by reactor pressure indicators and PCV-related variables. The most consistent fault is a hydrogen purge/vent control issue, specifically the H2 PCV (pressure control) subsystem not opening as commanded, causing elevated reactor pressure and related process responses.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations. The strongest rule-based hypotheses point to a fault in the H2 PCV (vent valve) path, most likely PCV stuck closed or PCV capacity degradation, causing reactor pressure buildup and abnormal vent/pressure signals. Upstream loop (R_PIC) is actively compensating, consistent with a PCV fault propagating through the CSTR vent and pressure signals.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with substantial deviation in correlations (high T²) and notable SPE (highly abnormal correlations), pointing toward an H2 vent actuator issue affecting reactor pressure. The rule-based hypotheses strongly point to a stuck H2 PCV (or degradation of PCV capacity) causing reactor pressure to rise and control loops to compensate abnormally.
PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by Hydrogen PCV dynamics, with PCV-related faults being most consistent with the evidence.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong contribution from reactor pressure and PCV-related variables; high T² and high SPE suggest a dominant process disturbance (likely H2 PCV issue) rather than a sensor-only fault.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with both T2 and SPE violated. The strongest evidence points to a condenser cooling issue driving the abnormal correlations, with possible H2 PCV-related faults contributing.

Abnormal PCA with both T² and SPE violations indicates a large, coherent upset rather than random sensor drift. Faults most consistent with the observed evidence are related to condenser cooling effectiveness and H2 PCV performance, with RB_LIC being a secondary contributor.

Normal operation PCA flagged abnormal. Evidence most strongly supports a condenser cooling problem driving the upset, with secondary evidence suggesting possible H2 PCV issues or related upstream effects.

PCA shows a large coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated, with strongest evidence pointing to a loss of condenser cooling effectiveness affecting downstream tray temperatures and column operation.

PCA flags coherent upset with reactor pressure rising and a saturated RB_LIC loop; likely H2 PCV issue propagating pressure rise, with RB_LIC saturation reinforcing the upset. Sensor/valve faults in PCV and RB_LIC are implicated; multiple faults may be active.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violated. The strongest rule-based hint is condenser cooling loss, with notable contributions from reboiler holdup and key control loops suggesting upstream compensation. Multiple faults may be present, but the top evidence points to condenser cooling effectiveness degradation as the primary issue, with possible PCV issues and reboiler/leakage contributing.

Abnormal PCA with large coherent upset (high T2 and high SPE) pointing to a process upset propagating through the CSTR/column system, with strongest evidence centering on reactor/PCV and reflux/condensing controls. Sensor- or actuator-related faults are possible given high SPE, but ruling out simple sensor fault without alarms suggests a process equipment/control issue.

Very large coherent upset with strong T² and SPE; RB_LIC loop is saturated and its PV is away from setpoint, indicating an actuator limiting/overriding condition likely driving the disturbance. Multiple faults could be contributing, but RB_LIC_out_of_range is most consistent with the evidence.

PCA flags a large, coherent upset with substantial deviation in multiple tray temperatures and acetone measurements, plus rising reactor/reboiler pressures. The rule-based evidence points to condenser cooling becoming ineffective, consistent with the high SPE and correlated temperature/concentration shifts. A catalyst activity loss is also plausible but less supported by the data. Sensor-only faults are less favored given the coherence of the upset, though one temperature sensor (tray_06_T) contributes notably to SPE.

PCA flags strong, coherent upset with large T² and high SPE, dominated by CSTR acetone-related measurements and reboiler holdup, plus control actions on BOT_TIC and TOP_TIC. This pattern aligns with process faults rather than sensor faults. Most likely multiple interacting faults causing reduced reactor performance and altered downstream feed to the column.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with significant SPE, dominated by acetone-related measurements and reactor holdups. Most likely a process-level degradation affecting reaction performance and downstream flow handling.
PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with significant load/processing shift. Most evidence points to a primary process degradation rather than a simple sensor fault.
High both Hotelling T2 and SPE with coherent disturbance; multiple faults involving the H2 PCV and catalyst may be driving the upset, with sensor bias also possible.

High coherence upset with large T² and large SPE indicating a process upset propagating normally; most evidence points to catalyst/activity loss and related CSTR outlet constraints, possibly with hydrogen vent valve issues.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with concurrent T2 and SPE violations. Saturation in the RB_LIC loop points to an actuator constraint being hit, with strong contribution from the reboiler loop and related CSTR holdup signals. The rule-based hypothesis most strongly supports RB_LIC_out_of_range, i.e., the RB_LIC loop output is saturated while PV is off the setpoint. Other plausible causes include process-level interactions (cstr_outlet capacity loss or cstr_liquid_leak) and catalyst/activity effects, but evidence centers on the reboiler control.

Abnormal PCA with large coherent upset (high T², high SPE) and a saturated RB_LIC loop. Most consistent with reduced CSTR outlet capacity causing reactor holdup rise and downstream effects, plus possible related feed/recirculation upset.

PCA detects a large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violations and an active column tray level alarm. The most consistent fault is a loss of CSTR outlet capacity causing altered holdup and acetone profile, with secondary issues related to reflux flow control affecting column operation.

PCA flags a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations and active column/tray/holdup alarms. Rule-based hints point toward a column/reflux disturbance with limited authority and a downstream up/downstream imbalance. The faults most consistent with the evidence are related to condenser/reflux performance and CSTR outlet capacity losses.
